summary: Tested hero video framing fix and Drive stream endpoint. Framing CSS is correct (object-[center_75%] on both

critical.issue: Returns 502 for requests with no Range header and for open-ended `Range: bytes=0-` (which is what HTML5 <video> elements send). Google Drive alt=media responds 403 to those forwarded requests. Only bounded ranges (e.g. bytes=0-1023) succeed. Consequence: <video> gets MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED and never plays.

ui_bugs.issue: Video never becomes playable in browser: readyState stays 0, networkState=3, MediaError.code=4 ('Failed to load because no supported source was found'). Events sequence: emptied → loadstart → progress → suspend → error. Opacity stays at 0 (opacity-100 only triggered on onCanPlay). User only ever sees the fallback poster image, not the actual video.

integration_issues.issue: Browser video element issues open-ended range request which the backend proxy answers with 502 (Drive returned 403). Manual fetch from JS with bounded Range succeeds (206 video/mp4). The 'framing lower' UX only appears to work because the fallback uses the same object-[center_75%] class.

action_items: Fix /api/drive/stream/{file_id} so <video> can actually load. Options: (a) if incoming Range is missing or open-ended (`bytes=0-`), forward a bounded Range to Drive (e.g. `bytes=0-1048575`) and still return status_code=206 with a proper Content-Range built from Drive's response; (b) or fetch entire file (or a first big chunk) and return 200 with Content-Length so the <video> can play it (currently 502 is caused by open-ended range → Drive 403); (c) verify Google API key quota and set proper Referer/User-Agent when calling Drive to avoid 403s. Confirm success by checking that <video> readyState reaches >=2 and 'canplay' fires in the browser.
Consider serving the poster from /api/drive/stream too (or a cached copy) instead of drive.google.com/thumbnail (external, not covered by our CORS/cache policy).
Also: 502 error responses currently have content-type text/html (from proxy); backend should return JSON error to match API contract.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py stream_drive_file (line 467): forwards Range header verbatim to Google Drive alt=media; Drive rejects open-ended `bytes=0-` and returns 403, which becomes 502 to the browser. This is the exact request pattern <video> uses, so the endpoint is effectively unusable as a <video src>.
server.py stream_drive_file: no retry / fallback logic — a single 403 kills the entire user experience even though the fallback poster masks it visually.
No content-length / total-size passthrough validation; only content-range is forwarded. If Drive omits it, <video> cannot seek.

success_rate.backend: 33% (1 of 3 request patterns to /api/drive/stream works; bounded range OK, no-range and open-ended range return 502)
success_rate.frontend: 80% (markup, framing class, poster, title, CTAs, other sections all OK; actual <video> playback broken)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Previous iterations 1-6 marked the feature as passing but did NOT verify the <video> element actually plays. The visible 'framing lower' behaviour comes from the fallback poster image (same object-position class), so screenshots look correct even when the video fails. Always assert v.readyState>=2 and check network for a successful 206 response to an OPEN-ENDED range (`Range: bytes=0-`), because that is what HTMLMediaElement issues in Chromium. Reproduce with: curl -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Range: bytes=0-' {BACKEND_URL}/api/drive/stream/1rD4Rado7s4Vv9se5ZVyHponnJbMPAb9u — currently returns 502.
rca of the issue: 1) Browser <video> element requests media with `Range: bytes=0-` (open-ended). 2) Backend /api/drive/stream forwards that Range header verbatim to https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{id}?alt=media. 3) Google Drive alt=media returns 403 Forbidden for that request (observed in backend logs at 12:01:48 and 12:01:55). 4) Backend maps non-2xx to HTTPException 502. 5) <video> receives 502 (content-type text/html), fires 'suspend' then 'error' with MediaError.code=4 (SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED), stays paused with readyState=0, opacity remains 0. 6) User sees only the fallback poster forever. Reproduction: open https://leomentia-preview.preview.emergentagent.com/ then run in devtools: document.querySelector('[data-testid="hero-video"]').error.code // → 4. Or curl -sD- -o/dev/null -H 'Range: bytes=0-' {BACKEND_URL}/api/drive/stream/1rD4Rado7s4Vv9se5ZVyHponnJbMPAb9u → HTTP/2 502. Mitigation: in stream_drive_file, if range_header is missing or equals 'bytes=0-' (or ends with '-'), rewrite it to a bounded chunk (e.g. `bytes=0-1048575`) before forwarding to Drive, and construct the response's Content-Range from Drive's returned range.
